place: Castro de Vila Nova de São Pedro (Chalcolithic fortified settlement, Azambuja), hilltop clearing ~25-30 m SSE of the 'Reduto Central' citadel
evidence: Timber crib retaining structure (planks + diagonal struts, rubble fill behind) against a wall face at yaw 104-122: the 2023 VNSP3000 report (Arqueologia & História 74-75, museuarqueologicodocarmo.pt R6_VNSP23) describes exactly this, a 'estrutura de madeira de contenção da parede' with 'rachão' fill installed Nov-Dec 2023 on the walls W, N and E of the Reduto Central

Excavated Chalcolithic-type limestone rubble walls, curvilinear structures and collapsed rampart banks on a hilltop; wild olive and lentisk scrub, dry July grass; VNSP digs run in July (3-21 July 2023 campaign)

Distant ridge at bearing ~253-275 deg, ~+1.9 deg after tilt correction, matches Serra de Montejunto in the GLO-90 DEM (bearing ~255 deg, 19-20 km, +1.6 deg); the northern lowland horizon also matches the DEM
Sun at yaw -111.7, pitch 63.5 vs predicted az 126.1 / el 65.3: camera tilted ~2.4 deg (world-up toward yaw -152); tilt-corrected heading of yaw 0 = 234.4 deg (naive 237.8)
PE-Core search of the Commons landmark gallery (hypothesis only) ranked VNSP's photo Q1792866 (cos 0.72-0.75) among the top hits in several views

Esri imagery: hilltop clearing with scattered trees around the polygonal citadel; citadel interior and the far (N) wall with the timber at bearings ~325-356 put the camera ~27 m SSE of the citadel centre (39.219745, -8.840397), with olive trees within 3-8 m to the S/SW/E and the access track below to the ESE
method: Ruled out mapped PT/W-Spain archaeological sites by DEM skyline matching (GLO-90 horizons vs extracted skyline, camera tilt solved from the sun); compared Commons gallery photos (contact sheets + PE-Core retrieval); the VNSP report's timber 'contenção' at the Reduto Central confirmed the site; camera placed from bearings to the citadel and nearby trees on Esri z19 imagery (pre-2023 imagery, so the timber itself is not visible on it). Residual: SSE horizon ~1 deg lower than the DEM predicts.

place: Unidentified rural plateau edge, probably west-central Portugal (limestone massifs of Serras de Aire e Candeeiros / Sico, Leiria-Santarem-Coimbra); regional estimate only
evidence: 2026-08-12 18:43 UTC is about 14 min after the maximum of the 12 August 2026 total solar eclipse (totality in N Spain and NE Portugal, ~18:28-18:31 UTC; deep partial elsewhere in Iberia). A small group sits in camping chairs facing the low western sun with a camera on a tripod: almost certainly eclipse watchers (not Perseids, which need darkness)

Shot from a car roof on a stick: the camera's own shadow (end of the stick shadow, yaw 47.0, pitch -8.84) gives the exact anti-solar direction -> sun at yaw -133.0, camera-frame elevation 8.84 deg; the saturated bloom centre agrees in yaw

Camera levelling checked on other shots from the same camera: the Leiria keep in IMG_20260813_122023_00_707 (residual rotation ~0.3 deg) and the flat field horizon in IMG_20260922_172452_00_779 are level. Taking 417 as level, the true sun elevation is 8.8 +- ~0.5 deg (clock good to ~5 min per the first-set Leiria/Cobrao checks). That band runs through western Portugal (e.g. ~-8.3..-9.3 deg lon at 38-40 N) and western Galicia

Conflicting evidence: the 360 deg skyline is a near-perfect 2.6 deg sinusoid (W low, E high) and the telecom mast at yaw 114 leans ~2.9 deg as a 2.6 deg tilt toward the sun would predict. Taken literally, that puts the true sun at ~11.4 deg, which is impossible anywhere in Iberia at 18:43 UTC, so the skyline is read as terrain (camera on a west-facing slope with an open, low western horizon, typical of an eclipse viewing spot)
Tilt-free check: the sun stands 11.1 deg above the skyline directly beneath it (skyline at about -2.3 deg in the camera frame)

Scene: gravel (limestone-grey) service road with a metal guardrail and a chain-link fence with angled-top posts; beyond the fence a grey crushed-stone/rockfill slope with a berm, a track at its toe and a flat pale floor (quarry benches, dump or embankment, seen against the sun); plain white tapered concrete boundary markers east of the road; red-orange gravelly soil in the road cut; dry grass with scattered oaks; plateau with cereal stubble and a green vineyard-like plot to the E; dense green hedge/plantation to the SW; lattice telecom mast with an equipment shelter ~0.4-0.6 km to the S (bearing ~170); HV pylons on a forested ridge to the NW (bearings ~334-340); no wind turbines anywhere on the skyline

DEM (Copernicus GLO-90) skyline matching: a brute-force search over the sun band (566k points), a tilt-aware NW-Iberia search (279k), searches around 483 solar plants, 114 dams and 800 OSM quarries/landfills. Best level-camera fits around quarries: Serra dos Candeeiros west-scarp limestone quarries (RMS 0.56 deg, predicted sun 8.95 deg) and Sico quarries near Pombal/Ansiao (RMS 0.79-0.75, sun 8.80). The specific Candeeiros quarries were rejected because wind turbines stand next to them and none appear in the panorama; the Sico ones because their road/pit layout does not match
method: Camera-shadow anti-solar point for sun yaw and elevation; NOAA solar model validated against the published eclipse figures (Lugo 11.2 deg at maximum, Guadramil 10.0 deg). Camera levelling calibrated on other shots from the same camera. Sun-band and tilt-free sun-minus-skyline constraints. Copernicus GLO-90 horizon profiles compared with the extracted 360 deg skyline over grid searches (level and tilt-aware) and targeted searches around OSM solar plants, dams, quarries and landfills (local PT/ES pbf extracts). Esri imagery checks of the best candidates: Alamos reservoir, Cabeco Santo PV plant, Caveira and Lousal mines, Montargil, Magos and Venda Velha dams, Candeeiros quarries A-D, Sico quarries, Maceira. None matched in detail. Estimate placed at the centre of the karst belt the evidence favours (between the Candeeiros best fits, Sico and Leiria)
